description: Item 5: full layout overhaul. Remove the top bar entirely. Introduce a single persistent left sidebar on ALL authenticated pages with a fixed item order, an unread-notification indicator, a light/dark theme slide toggle above the footer, and a footer showing the profile (icon/name/banner/streak) that links to the profile page plus a logout button. Make the Painel/Dashboard the application's main/home page and rebuild it with a horizontal Duolingo-style trail (square module nodes, circular lesson nodes) that can be dragged/scrolled behind the overlay components, clickable nodes (view lesson info / do the lesson / show completion), a bottom carousel to switch modules of the selected course, a top-right button opening a 'top-down' panel, and a top-left courses/rooms selector that swaps the trail and changes the top-down panel contents (courses: friends rank by PAC in that course + global daily missions; rooms: room rank when enabled + room tasks/missions, with a notice board in the bottom-right).
steps: SIDEBAR (AppShell): Rewrite src/components/layout/AppShell.tsx to remove the <header> top bar (which currently holds the Athen name, NotificationBell, profile name, and the Sair button). Build a single persistent left sidebar used on every authenticated page (AppShell already wraps all authenticated routes via <Outlet/> in src/App.tsx). Keep the existing responsive collapse-to-drawer behavior for small viewports (<=768px) but move the hamburger toggle into the sidebar/content area, not a top bar.

SIDEBAR header + item order: At the top of the sidebar show the brand icon + platform name 'Athen' (reuse BrandMark/Logo), linking to the Painel. Then the nav items in EXACTLY this order: Painel (/dashboard), Catálogo (/catalog), Salas (/rooms), Ranking (/ranking), Amigos (/friends), Cadernos (/notebook), Notificações (/notifications), Configurações (/settings). Keep the admin-only CRUD link available to admins but placed so it does not disturb the required order (e.g. after Configurações). Note 'Cadernos' label (plural) per the spec even though the route is /notebook.

SIDEBAR notification indicator: The Notificações item must show a visual indicator when there is at least one unread notification. Reuse the existing unread-count hook useUnreadCount (src/features/notifications/api.ts) and the formatUnreadBadge helper (src/features/notifications/helpers.ts); render a small badge/dot on the Notificações nav item. The old standalone NotificationBell lived in the top bar — fold its unread logic into the sidebar item (you may keep NotificationBell as a small reusable badge or inline the hook). Do not break the existing notifications polling.

SIDEBAR theme toggle: Just above the footer, add a slide-style button that toggles the page theme between light and dark. Implement theming with a data attribute on the root (e.g. document.documentElement.dataset.theme = 'dark'|'light') and add a [data-theme=dark] palette override block in src/styles/theme.css (dark values for --color-bg, --color-surface, --color-border, --color-text, --color-text-muted; keep brand purple/gold readable). Persist the choice in localStorage and initialize from it (fallback to light or prefers-color-scheme). Keep it a small self-contained module/hook (e.g. a useTheme hook under src/components/layout/ or src/lib/) so it is testable; a pure helper (resolveInitialTheme / nextTheme) with a unit test under __tests__ is preferred.

SIDEBAR footer: In the sidebar footer show the current user's profile: avatar icon, display name, a small banner accent, and the streak (reuse profile from useAuth(); streak_count with the 🔥 convention used elsewhere). The whole profile area links to /profile (the own profile). Add a logout button (reuse the existing signOut flow + toast + navigate('/login') from the old header). Keep accessibility (aria-labels).

ROUTING - Painel as home: Make the Painel/Dashboard the application's main page. In src/App.tsx keep '/' as the public LandingPage for logged-out users, but ensure that an authenticated user's primary destination is the dashboard: add an index redirect so an authenticated user landing on an app entry goes to /dashboard, and point the brand/home link at /dashboard. Do NOT remove the public landing/auth routes. If you add a redirect, guard it so public routes still work for anonymous users.

DASHBOARD rebuild (trail): Rebuild src/features/dashboard/DashboardPage.tsx so the central area is a horizontal Duolingo-style trail for the selected course: module nodes rendered as SQUARES and lesson nodes as CIRCLES, laid out left-to-right in course order. The trail must be horizontally draggable/scrollable (pointer/touch drag + wheel/overflow scroll) and sits BEHIND the overlay UI (sidebar, selector, top-down panel, carousel) using z-index/absolute layering. Reuse useCourseTrail(userId, courseId) (src/features/dashboard/api.ts) for modules/lessons with completed + locked flags. Each node is clickable: clicking a lesson node opens lesson info and lets the user do the lesson (navigate to /lesson/:id, which is the existing overlay runner) and clearly shows completion state (completed vs available vs locked, e.g. check/lock styling). Keep locked lessons non-navigable. Preserve the server-authoritative data; no fake completion state.

DASHBOARD module carousel: Add a carousel at the BOTTOM that lets the user switch between the modules of the selected course (changes which module's lessons are focused/scrolled-to in the trail). Drive it from the selected course's modules (from useCourseTrail). Selecting a module scrolls/snaps the trail to that module.

DASHBOARD top-right top-down panel: Add a button in the TOP-RIGHT of the dashboard that opens a 'top-down' panel (a panel that slides down from the top) showing context-specific info. Its contents depend on the courses/rooms selector (next step).

DASHBOARD top-left courses/rooms selector: Add a selector in the TOP-LEFT that switches between 'Cursos' and 'Salas' mode. In Cursos mode: the trail shows the selected course's trail, and the top-down panel shows the friends ranking by PAC for that course (reuse FriendsCourseRanking / useFriendsCoursePac from src/features/rankings) PLUS global daily missions. In Salas mode: the trail shows the selected room's course trail (reuse useRoomContent / room data from src/features/rooms/api.ts; a room links to a course), the top-down panel shows the room ranking (when enabled per the room's pac_visibility; reuse useRoomMembers) and the room tasks/missions (useMissions), and a notice board (useAnnouncements) is shown in the BOTTOM-RIGHT. Provide a course picker (user enrollments) in Cursos mode and a room picker (useMyRooms) in Salas mode to choose which trail is shown.

DAILY MISSIONS (global): The spec references 'missões diárias globais' in Cursos mode. There is no existing global daily-missions table (missions are room-scoped). Implement a minimal, honest representation: derive lightweight daily goals from existing server-authoritative data (e.g. 'estude uma aula hoje' from completions/last_study_date, 'mantenha a sequência' from streak_count). Keep it clearly client-derived display (no fake XP). Put the derivation in a pure helper with a unit test. If true global daily missions would require a new backend table, do NOT invent XP-granting backend behavior; implement the display-only version and note the limitation in findings.

STYLES: Add the needed layout/trail/overlay/carousel/top-down-panel/notice-board styles to src/styles/theme.css (or a scoped style block), using CSS variables so dark theme works. Ensure the trail layer sits behind overlay components and the page remains responsive. Reuse existing --radius/--shadow/brand vars.

Keep all pt-BR copy and the required sidebar item order and labels exactly. Remove now-dead code paths from the old top-bar header, but keep NotificationBell if you reuse its badge. Run npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm run test, npm run build after the changes and fix any regressions. Do not introduce new lint warnings beyond the 6 pre-existing ones.
acceptance_criteria: There is no top bar; the old header (platform name + notification bell + profile name + Sair) is gone and all authenticated pages render only the left sidebar + content.

The sidebar is persistent across all authenticated routes and lists, in order: Athen brand, Painel, Catálogo, Salas, Ranking, Amigos, Cadernos, Notificações, Configurações (admin CRUD may follow for admins).
The Notificações sidebar item shows a visual unread indicator when unread notifications exist (driven by useUnreadCount).
A light/dark slide toggle sits just above the footer, actually switches the theme (via [data-theme=dark] in theme.css), and persists across reloads.
The sidebar footer shows the profile avatar/name/banner/streak linking to /profile and includes a working logout button.
An authenticated user's main page is the Painel/Dashboard (brand/home links go to /dashboard; authenticated entry resolves to the dashboard).

The dashboard renders a horizontal Duolingo-style trail with SQUARE module nodes and CIRCLE lesson nodes, is horizontally draggable/scrollable behind the overlay UI, and lesson nodes are clickable to view/do a lesson and show completion/locked state (data from useCourseTrail).

A bottom module carousel switches between the selected course's modules; a top-right button opens a top-down panel; a top-left Cursos/Salas selector swaps the trail and the top-down panel contents as specified (Cursos: friends PAC rank + daily missions; Salas: room rank when enabled + room missions + a bottom-right notice board).
npm run typecheck, npm run test, npm run build pass; npm run lint has 0 errors and no more than the 6 pre-existing warnings.
verification: export PATH="/opt/toolchains/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.3/bin:$PATH" && npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run test && npm run build

Read src/components/layout/AppShell.tsx and src/features/dashboard/DashboardPage.tsx to confirm the sidebar structure/order, notification indicator, theme toggle, profile footer, and the trail/carousel/top-down-panel/selector/notice-board.
grep -n 'data-theme' src/styles/theme.css to confirm the dark palette override exists.
